summary: Report No. 27 of South Korean Interim Government Activities, prepared by the National Economic Board for USAMGIK, covering December 1947 (with November data for transportation, communications, finance and several other sections). It records a month dominated by an acute electric power shortage after North Korea cut supply on 25 November, falling coal, textile and paper output, and food supply concerns despite rice collection reaching 96.2 per cent of quota. Politically it covers the assassination of Chang Duk Soo, the founding of the National Independence Federation, Rhee and Kim Koo's rightist merger, preparation for the UN Commission, and Legislative Assembly disputes with the executive. Tables give prices, trade, finance, refugees (163,253 entered in 1947), and vested property disposal, while the interzone section summarizes North Korean and Soviet radio. Historians will find it useful for the economic statistics and the occupation's own view of politics.
highlights: North Korea cut electric power on 25 November 1947, capping South Korea's draw at 80,000 KW; December deliveries fell to 68 million KWH, and an Emergency Electric Power Board was set up with legal powers and heating bans.

Rice collection reached 96.2 per cent of quota by late December 1947 (232,213 metric tons collected), though Cholla-pukto lagged at 77 per cent and imports of 10,000-34,000 tons monthly are needed to last past July 1948.

Seoul's composite retail price index stood at 1,936 in December 1947, over 19 times the August 1945 base, while the wholesale index rose to 7,066, driven by coal and power shortages and rice-collection loans.
Chang Duk Soo, Korean Democratic Party head, was assassinated on 3 December; police were ordered out of politics, youth groups restrained, and Gen. Hodge and Military Governor Dean issued statements.
The moderate National Independence Federation of 15 parties held its first meeting on 20 December under Kimm Kiu Sic, while the announced Rhee Syngman and Kim Koo merger stalled.

The power shortage cut output: November cotton yarn fell 13.2 per cent, paper 22.2 per cent and flour 24.3 per cent in vested mills, mines ran about 18 per cent under quota, and 58 trains were removed.

Ordinance No. 160 created the Agricultural Improvement Service on 15 December, and the Legislative Assembly marked its first anniversary on 12 December after settling its veto dispute with Gen. Helmick.
163,253 refugees from North Korea were counted in 1947 against 185,441 in 1946; December's 4,487 was the lowest since February 1947, and about 60 per cent settled in Seoul or Kyonggi-do.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of Report No. 27 (December 1947), prepared by the National Economic Board for USAMGIK, with a map of the U.S. and U.S.S.R. zones and contents for Parts I-VI.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Notes that most data are for December, but transportation, communications, industrial production, mining and trade carry November figures. Admits provincial statistics are unreliable, non-economic data thin, and the report largely American-authored.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Covers refugees from North Korea (163,253 in 1947) and Office of Property Custody work, including 285 companies under investigation and 16 vested-property sales worth 5,205 thousand won.

sections.title: Section 1: Population
sections.summary: December refugee arrivals from the north were 4,487, the lowest since February 1947; the 1947 total was 163,253 against 185,441 in 1946. About 60 per cent went to Seoul or Kyonggi-do. Also 21,916 illegal Japan entrants.

sections.title: Section 2: Office of Property Custody (Vested Property)
sections.summary: A Corporate Reorganization Sub-section began, with 285 companies under investigation. Loans guaranteed reached 235 million won; 16 sales totaled 5,205 thousand won. Royal Family estates pass to SKIG control from 1 January 1948.

sections.title: Part II: Production and Supply
sections.summary: Rice collection reached 96.2 per cent of quota; Seoul's retail price index hit 1,936. Mining, textile and paper output fell amid power shortages, while 1947 civilian supply imports totaled 988,344 tons and 193 unions reported 58,556 members.

sections.title: Section 1: Food Supply
sections.summary: 232,213 metric tons of rice were collected, 35,038 distributed and 586,419 held. Collection reached 96.2 per cent of quota (Cholla-pukto 77 per cent). Imports of 10,000-34,000 tons monthly are needed to avoid exhausting stocks by July 1948.

sections.title: Section 2: Prices
sections.summary: Seoul's retail price index stood at 1,936 in December 1947, over 19 times August 1945; the wholesale index rose to 7,066. Tobacco prices rose 50-233 per cent on 15 December.

sections.title: Section 3: Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries
sections.summary: Sets 1948 goals of 3,211,844 chungbo cropped, with 1947 rice at 81.6 per cent of goal. Sericulture was cut by power shortages; 220,953 tons of fertilizer shipped. Ordinance 160 created the Agricultural Improvement Service on 15 December.

sections.title: Section 4: Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: November anthracite output fell 5.3 per cent from October; mines ran about 18 per cent under quota amid power, truck and tire shortages. Only 64,823 tons of bituminous came from Japan. Copper mines owed 42,208,455 won.

sections.title: Section 5: Industrial Production
sections.summary: Reports covered under 10 per cent of 2,012 factories. November flour fell 24.3 per cent, cotton yarn 13.2 per cent, cloth 15.7 per cent, paper 22.2 per cent and cigarettes 15 per cent; coal, pitch and power were short.

sections.title: Section 6: Allocations and Distribution
sections.summary: Surplus Army clothing is to be dyed at the Chosun Boseki plant at Pusanjin. The Federation of Financial Associations distributed 89,820,257 won of goods, and an emergency import of about 2,000,000 gallons of kerosene was ordered.

sections.title: Section 7: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Private imports in November were 463,123,673 won against exports of 107,700,696 won; Pusan handled 48.2 per cent of imports. About 570 tons of scheelite sailed for the U.S. Civilian Supply imports in 1947 totaled 988,344 tons.

sections.title: Section 8: Labor
sections.summary: The Department of Labor planned a four-bureau reorganization. Power-shortage orders suspended child labor and hours laws. The Kyongsang Textile dispute over seven discharged union men stalled; 193 unions had 58,556 members.

sections.title: Part III: Public Services
sections.summary: Railroads removed 58 trains in November for lack of coal; North Korea's 25 November power cut limited deliveries to 68 million KWH in December. Also covers communications, public works and the 40-house Seoul housing project.

sections.title: Section 1: Transportation
sections.summary: Lack of bituminous coal forced removal of 58 trains in November. Department receipts fell 21 per cent and expenditures 12 per cent; under 38 per cent of locomotives were operable. Marine income rose 44 per cent.

sections.title: Section 2: Communications
sections.summary: Communications receipts rose 18 per cent in November, led by a 7.3 million won rise in telephone income after the 1 October rate increase. About 41,000,000 Japanese stamps were ordered destroyed.

sections.title: Section 3: Public Utilities
sections.summary: After North Korea's 25 November notice capping South Korea's draw at 80,000 KW, power delivered fell to 68 million KWH in December (52 million from the north). An Emergency Electric Power Board set priorities and banned heating and cooking use.

sections.title: Section 4: Public Works
sections.summary: December was the low point for Public Works: man-days fell to 72,633 and wages to 14.5 million won. Andong and Namchang bridge projects began, and 248 fires cost 244.7 million won.

sections.title: Section 5: Housing
sections.summary: The 40-house low-cost Seoul project was finished and occupied; a site for 1,000 houses is planned. Refugee houses under the Welfare Housing Plan reached 5,736 of 15,730 planned, and 200 winterized tents were occupied.

sections.title: Part IV: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosun note issue reached 33,388 million won; November deposits rose 2,569 million and loans 16.2 billion, mostly for rice collection. Eight supplemental appropriations of 629 million won raised the budget to 20,089 million.

sections.title: Section 1: Government Finance
sections.summary: Note issue reached 33,388 million won, driven by rice-collection loans of 11,772 million. Eight supplemental appropriations of 629 million won raised the budget to 20,089 million. November revenue was 1,225 million won.

sections.title: Section 2: Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: November deposits rose 2,569 million won and loans 16.2 billion, mostly for rice collection. Directives tightened loan renewals; a deposit drive added 2.5 billion won. A scheelite shipment near US$750,000 was sent.

sections.title: Part V: Government and Politics
sections.summary: Covers the Legislative Assembly's dispute with Gen. Helmick over vetoes, the 3 December assassination of Chang Duk Soo, the 20 December National Independence Federation, the stalled Rhee-Kim Koo merger and interzone radio.

sections.title: Section 1: Administration
sections.summary: Legislative Assembly relations with Deputy Military Governor Helmick over his vetoes were stormy, then smoothed. Civil Service held 4,108 clerical examinations and abolished 383 Seoul positions.

sections.title: Section 2: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: KILA settled its dispute with Gen. Helmick over vetoed bills and approved governors of Kangwon-do and Chungchong-namdo. The Land Reform Bill (3 chungbo ceiling) had its first reading; a no-confidence motion failed 35 to 27.

sections.title: Section 3: Political Developments
sections.summary: The moderate National Independence Federation of 15 parties was founded 20 December under Kimm Kiu Sic. Rhee Syngman and Kim Koo announced a merger in principle that stalled; parties split over a South-only election.

sections.title: Section 4: Legal Affairs
sections.summary: Ordinances 158-160 and Executive Order No. 9 were published. Prison population stood at 20,718. A rightist terrorism case went to a military commission and the Chang Duk Soo assassination was referred.

sections.title: Section 5: Police
sections.summary: After Chang Duk Soo's assassination on 3 December, police were ordered to stay out of politics and youth groups were restrained. Rice-collection resisters were arrested; weekly fingerprint requests fell from about 5,000 to 1,760-2,889.

sections.title: Section 6: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Mail was exchanged at Tosang on 13 and 27 December. Radio Pyongyang hailed North Korea's currency conversion and rejected the UN decision; Radio Moscow denounced the UN Commission and MacArthur's Japan policy.

sections.title: Part VI: Social
sections.summary: Covers health, education, culture, public information, press and Korean National Youth, including a 3,128,979,081-won education budget request and youth membership of 404,585 by December 1947.

sections.title: Section 1: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: The National Venereal Disease Center opened in Seoul on 3 December with 65 beds. Typhus fell from 117 cases to 4 and typhoid from 239 to 24 against December 1946. A nutrition survey covered 4,676 families.

sections.title: Section 2: Education
sections.summary: The 1948-49 budget request was 3,128,979,081 won, nearly 80 percent for common schools, against 1,660,242,480 won the year before. Provincial advisors met 16-17 December on school taxation; teacher certification rules start 1 January 1948.

sections.title: Section 3: Culture
sections.summary: The National Library logged 291,285 books used and 265,275 readers in 1947. Seven Koreans left to study in the United States and four in Nanking; the Korean Broadcasting System aired 337 hours.

sections.title: Section 4: Public Information
sections.summary: The Department issued 74 press releases in December, including statements by Dean and Hodge on the Chang Duk Soo murder. The Public Opinion Bureau registered 4 parties and 9 publications; a Nonsan trip found 35.8 percent saw U.S. benefit.

sections.title: Section 5: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: The press covered the Helmick-KILA veto dispute, Dean's transfer of the Dai Han Min Chung terror case to a military court, and the failed Rhee-Kim Koo accord. The Chang Duk Soo murder overshadowed all, prompting press curbs.

sections.title: Section 6: Korean National Youth, Inc.
sections.summary: Membership grew from 19,270 in January to 404,585 in December 1947, with 15,304 leaders. Lee Bum Suk and Dai Dong's leader issued an 11 December appeal against mutual slander; 11,843,113 seedlings were planted.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: Blank scanned pages marked as digitized by Google, a library barcode and date-due slip stamped 23 June 2020, and a back cover image. No report content.
